question: Why did workers who refused to save more today happily agree to save more out of future pay rises?
answer: Because the cost fell on a later self. In Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi's Save More Tomorrow plan, contributions rose only with each pay rise, so take-home pay never fell. Average saving rates went from 3.5% to 13.6% in about three and a half years. The present self signs; the future self pays.
move: Let your future self sign up for what your present self keeps refusing.
ask: What good habit could I set up now so that it starts after my next pay rise or birthday?
source: Thaler & Benartzi, Journal of Political Economy, 2004
reference: Thaler & Benartzi, Save More Tomorrow: Using Behavioral Economics to Increase Employee Saving, Journal of Political Economy 112 (S1), 2004
